macro_markets.query: What are the most important macroeconomic and stock market news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major index movements, Fed/central bank news, and significant company earnings or announcements.

crypto_news.query: What are the most significant cryptocurrency and blockchain news from the past 24 hours? Include major price movements, regulatory news, and notable project developments.

items.title: Bitcoin climbs above $63K as easing oil prices lift risk appetite
items.summary: Bitcoin rose above $63,000 in the past 24 hours, with market commentary linking the move to easing oil prices and improved risk appetite. Crypto market trackers also showed BTC trading around $63.2K, up about 1.6% on the day.

items.title: Bitcoin whales push BTC toward $64K as Coinbase premium strengthens
items.summary: Cointelegraph reported that Bitcoin whales helped drive BTC toward $64,000 as the Coinbase Premium broke a key level, suggesting stronger U.S. demand. This points to accumulation activity rather than a purely macro-driven move.

items.title: Bitcoin drops 3% amid U.S.-Iran tensions and leverage flush
items.summary: CoinMarketCap’s market coverage said Bitcoin fell about 3% during the day on renewed U.S.-Iran tensions and roughly $300 million in crypto liquidations. The move highlights how geopolitical risk and leverage unwinds are still shaping short-term crypto prices.

items.title: XRP rises as SWIFT taps Ripple-linked banks for blockchain payments
items.summary: crypto.news reported that XRP gained after SWIFT moved to work with banks linked to Ripple for blockchain-based payments. The story adds fresh momentum to the ongoing institutional payments narrative around Ripple and XRP.

items.title: Paul Grewal exits Coinbase legal helm ahead of key CLARITY vote
items.summary: crypto.news said Coinbase’s top legal executive Paul Grewal is leaving before a crucial vote on the CLARITY Act. The timing makes the move notable because U.S. crypto market-structure legislation is entering a sensitive stage.

items.title: Trump White House rejects SEC snub claims before CLARITY showdown
items.summary: crypto.news reported that the White House pushed back on claims that the SEC had been sidelined ahead of the CLARITY Act debate. The update underscores ongoing regulatory tension around which agencies will shape crypto oversight.

items.title: Hong Kong SFC forces crypto platforms to drop SMS authentication
items.summary: crypto.news reported that Hong Kong’s Securities and Futures Commission is requiring crypto platforms to stop using SMS-based authentication. The rule reflects a broader push for stronger security controls across regulated crypto venues.

items.title: Bitdeer unveils $36 million Nevada factory to expand Bitcoin mining
items.summary: crypto.news said Bitdeer is opening a $36 million factory in Nevada, signaling continued investment in Bitcoin mining infrastructure. The development is significant because it expands hardware and manufacturing capacity in the sector.

items.title: Ethereum Foundation explains why AI still struggles to find real bugs
items.summary: crypto.news reported that the Ethereum Foundation published an explanation for why AI systems still fail to reliably identify real software bugs. The piece is relevant to blockchain development because it highlights limits in AI-assisted auditing and security tooling.

items.title: PayPal expands PYUSD to Polygon’s Open Money Stack
items.summary: crypto.news said PayPal is bringing its PYUSD stablecoin to Polygon’s Open Money Stack. The move is notable as another step in stablecoin integration across mainstream payment and blockchain infrastructure.

ai_news.query: What are the most important artificial intelligence and machine learning news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include new model releases, company announcements, research breakthroughs, and industry trends.

items.title: OpenAI launches ChatGPT Work for workplace automation
items.summary: OpenAI unveiled ChatGPT Work, an agent designed to execute tasks across different applications and files, signaling a stronger push into professional AI tools and office automation. Reuters frames the launch as part of intensifying competition with Anthropic and others in enterprise AI.

items.title: Meta opens developer access to Muse Spark 1.1
items.summary: Meta released developer access to its Muse Spark AI model and an upgraded version, expanding availability beyond internal use. Reuters says the move puts Meta more directly against OpenAI and Anthropic in commercial AI model offerings.

items.title: OpenAI launches GPT-Live voice models
items.summary: OpenAI introduced GPT-Live, a new family of real-time voice models that can listen and speak simultaneously. The release adds another multimodal capability to OpenAI’s product line and highlights growing competition in low-latency voice AI.

items.title: xAI launches Grok 4.5 for coding and agentic tasks
items.summary: xAI released Grok 4.5, describing it as its most intelligent model yet and positioning it for coding and agent-style workflows. Reuters reports the model was launched on Wednesday and is intended to strengthen xAI’s presence in advanced assistant and developer use cases.

items.title: Anthropic adds Ben Bernanke to Long-Term Benefit Trust
items.summary: Anthropic appointed former U.S. Federal Reserve chair Ben Bernanke to its Long-Term Benefit Trust, an oversight body tied to the company’s public mission. Reuters says the appointment is meant to reinforce governance and long-term alignment as Anthropic scales.

items.title: New copyright fight escalates around OpenAI
items.summary: The New York Times and other newspapers asked a federal court to sanction OpenAI, alleging the company misled the court about its ability to search internal systems for evidence in a copyright dispute. Reuters reports the filing comes amid a high-stakes legal battle over training data and news content.

items.title: Italy fines Character.AI owner over data protection breaches
items.summary: Italy’s data protection authority fined Character Technologies, the owner of Character.AI, €158,000 for breaches of data protection rules. Reuters says the penalty underscores continued regulatory scrutiny of consumer-facing AI platforms in Europe.

items.title: Micron plans more than $250 billion in U.S. investment tied to AI chip demand
items.summary: Micron said it plans to invest more than $250 billion in the United States through 2035, citing surging AI-era demand for memory chips. Reuters notes the announcement aligns with broader U.S. efforts to expand domestic semiconductor production.

gaming.query: What are the most notable video game and gaming industry news from the past 24 hours? Include game releases, announcements, esports, and industry developments.

items.title: Call of Duty: Black Ops 1 and 2 ports arrive on PS4 and PS5
items.summary: IGN reports that ports of Call of Duty: Black Ops and Black Ops 2 are now available on PlayStation 4 and PlayStation 5, marking a notable release for console shooters. The launch is being discussed alongside concerns about the pricing and overall value of the ports.

items.title: Assassin’s Creed Black Flag Resynced sets a new series peak on Steam
items.summary: IGN says Assassin’s Creed Black Flag Resynced reached around 100,000 concurrent players on Steam, the biggest peak for the franchise so far. The strong start makes it one of the day’s most notable PC release stories.

items.title: Pokémon Go marks its 10th anniversary with a live event
items.summary: IGN is covering a live Pokémon Go anniversary livestream as the game celebrates 10 years with special announcements and surprises. This is one of the clearest major mobile gaming events in the latest coverage.

items.title: Nintendo confirms Mario Kart Tour will shut down in September
items.summary: IGN reports that Nintendo will end service for Mario Kart Tour after seven years, with no offline version planned. The shutdown is a significant mobile gaming and live-service industry development.

items.title: Xbox leadership says Game Pass growth fell short of expectations
items.summary: IGN reports that Xbox CEO Asha Sharma acknowledged Game Pass has not grown as Microsoft expected, with reports suggesting it is far below prior subscriber targets. The story adds to broader scrutiny of Xbox’s subscription strategy.

items.title: Sony says new PlayStation discs will end in January 2028
items.summary: The Verge reports that Sony is ending physical PlayStation game discs for new releases after January 2028, moving the platform toward a digital-only future. The announcement is one of the biggest industry changes in recent coverage.

items.title: Epic Games settles lawsuit with former Fortnite leaker
items.summary: VGTimes reports that Epic Games has settled its lawsuit against a former Fortnite contractor accused of leaking unannounced collaborations. The company dropped its monetary claims, making this a notable legal and business development in the games industry.

items.title: The Crew Motorfest announced for Nintendo Switch 2
items.summary: VGTimes reports that Ubisoft has announced The Crew Motorfest will launch on Nintendo Switch 2 on October 8, 2026. The physical retail release will include a digital download code.

items.title: Frostpunk 2 reaches 1 million copies sold
items.summary: VGTimes reports that 11 bit studios says Frostpunk 2 has sold 1 million copies across all platforms. The milestone is one of the clearest sales highlights in the latest industry news cycle.

items.title: Xbox layoffs reportedly hit id Software and Obsidian
items.summary: VGC reports that Xbox layoffs have significantly affected id Software and cut dozens of developers at Obsidian. The report adds to a wider wave of restructuring across Microsoft’s gaming division.
